difficulty_reason: Prove Cech^p(K, I) = I(X) for p = 0 and 0 for p > 0 for an injective abelian sheaf I on a hypercovering K: first establish the chain of identifications F(Z) = prod F(U_i) = prod Mor(h_{U_i}, F) = Mor(F(Z), F) = Mor(Z_{F(Z)}, F) = Mor(Z_{F(Z)}^#, F) for Z in SR(C,X), giving s(F(K)) = Hom(s(Z_{F(K)}^#), F) (equation-identify-cech); lemma-hypercovering-acyclic makes s(Z_{F(K)}^#) quasi-isomorphic to Z_X^#; applying Hom(-, I) and injectivity of I gives that s(I(K)) is acyclic in positive degrees, so Cech^i(K,I) = 0 for i > 0; degree 0 is lemma-h0-cech.
